title: Hyderabad Marks Diwali in Many Ways, From Bommala Koluvu to Kali Puja
excerpt: On Sunday, November 8, Telugu doll displays, Bengali Kali Puja, Maharashtrian oil baths and traders' new-year pujas converge on the lit lanes around Charminar.
body:
• Diwali in Hyderabad falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, combining the Naraka Chaturdashi morning observance with the evening Lakshmi Puja — published Hyderabad guidance puts the puja window at about 6:07 p.m. to 8:08 p.m.
  • The city's celebration is many celebrations at once: Telugu families stage Bommala Koluvu doll displays, Bengali associations hold Kali Puja, Maharashtrian families begin with Vasu Baras and an oil bath, and trader communities perform puja for their account books.
  • The old city is the evening's centre: Charminar illuminated, Laad Bazaar's lac bangles and Begum Bazaar's wholesale diyas and dry fruits.
  • Practical note for visitors: Begum Bazaar's Sunday opening could not be confirmed — do bulk festival shopping on Friday or Saturday and check locally before a Sunday trip.

Hyderabad does not celebrate one Diwali. It celebrates a dozen of them on the same streets — a Telugu festival of doll displays and morning oil baths, a Bengali Kali Puja, a Maharashtrian Diwali that starts with Vasu Baras, and a traders' new year marked over fresh account books — all of it converging, on the evening of Sunday, November 8, on the lit lanes around Charminar.

One Sunday, two halves

In Hyderabad, Diwali 2026 carries both halves of the festival in a single day. The morning belongs to Naraka Chaturdashi: families take a pre-dawn oil bath, wear new clothes and mark Krishna's victory over Narakasura. The evening belongs to Lakshmi Puja, with published Hyderabad guidance putting the puja window at about 6:07 p.m. to 8:08 p.m. on November 8, and rows of earthen lamps — pramidalu — appearing at doorways and balconies across the city. Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6.

Telangana homes add a tradition of their own: Bommala Koluvu, the display of dolls arranged for the festival. "In Telangana, the tradition of Bommala Koluvu is cherished. Each year, I add new dolls from different states to our collection, which has been passed down through generations," Sudha, a homemaker from Kukatpally, told the Deccan Chronicle in its survey of the city's celebrations.

""In Telangana, the tradition of Bommala Koluvu is cherished."

Many communities, one festival

The Bengali community marks Diwali night with Kali Puja, organised by associations including Uttarayan, the Prabashi Socio-Cultural Association and the Hyderabad Bengali Swarna Shilpi Vivekananda Kali Mandir. Maharashtrian families begin earlier in the festival cycle. "We begin our celebrations with Vasu Baras (Gopadma Vrat) and take an abhyanga snan (oil bath) on Diwali day, which is believed to cleanse negativity," Ambarish Lahankar, founder of Mitraangan Maharashtrians of Hyderabad, said. Maharashtrian and Gujarati communities also organise Diwali melas during the season.

For Hyderabad's Gujarati, Marwadi and Sindhi trader communities, Diwali is also a financial new year: puja is performed for the account books that open the year's trading. And the festival's tail belongs to the Bihari community, whose Chhath Puja follows Diwali at water bodies across the city.

The old city after dark

For a visitor, the evening's route runs through the old city. Charminar — built in 1591 and illuminated in the evenings, according to Telangana Tourism — anchors streets strung with festival lights. West of the monument, Laad Bazaar sells its signature lac bangles, made in workshops behind the shops; Hyderabad lac bangles received Geographical Indication registration on March 1, 2024. Nearby, Begum Bazaar, the city's wholesale market near the Naya Pul bridge, supplies much of the festival itself: diyas by the dozen, puja materials, dry fruits and sweets for gifting.

Two cautions from Hyderabad's own Diwali guidance are worth carrying. Begum Bazaar's opening on Diwali Sunday could not be confirmed — guides disagree on its Sunday hours — so bulk buying is safer on Friday or Saturday. And fireworks are governed by the Supreme Court's standing order: only green or improved crackers, and only between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m., unless a stricter local order applies. The lamps, as the guidance notes, need no licence and no window.
